items.headline: 宇航员为何能看见月背的五次闪光？
items.headline_en: Five Tiny Flashes on the Moon’s Far Side
items.summary: NASA 11 月 17 日公布初步报告：阿耳忒弥斯二号在约 7.4 万公里外看到月背五次微弱闪光。当时月球挡住了太阳，暗背景让小岩块高速撞击月面的光更容易看见。这些观测有助于估计未来月面设施遭遇小撞击的频率。
items.summary_en: NASA’s 17 November report describes five faint flashes seen by Artemis II from about 74,000 km away. The Moon blocked the Sun, making light from small, fast-moving rocks striking the surface easier to see. The observations help estimate impact risks for future lunar facilities.

items.headline: 拉一拉，双层石墨烯的电阻就变了
items.summary: 11 月 12 日发表的研究把两层只有一个原子厚的碳片错开一个小角度，叠出莫尔条纹。研究者再用可伸缩的装置改变两层之间的相对形变，测到电阻明显变化。这让他们除了调温度和磁场，还能用拉伸来研究材料中的电子。
items.summary_en: In a study published on 12 November, two atom-thin carbon sheets were twisted to form a moiré pattern. A device changed how much one sheet stretched relative to the other, markedly changing the electrical resistance. Strain gives researchers another way to probe how electrons behave in the material.

items.headline: 无人机从座头鲸呼出的水雾里读出 DNA
items.headline_en: Drones Collect DNA from a Whale’s Breath
items.summary: 11 月 17 日发表的研究用无人机收集座头鲸呼出的水雾，从 26 头鲸取得 58 份样本，提取的 DNA 约 84% 来自鲸本身。同一头鲸的呼气样本和组织样本给出了吻合的结果。研究人员因此可以在不接触鲸的情况下研究种群的遗传多样性。
items.summary_en: A study published on 17 November collected 58 breath samples from 26 humpbacks using drones. About 84% of the extracted DNA came from whales. Breath and tissue samples from the same whale gave matching results, opening a way to study genetic diversity without touching the animals.

items.headline: 为什么有的断层在破裂前会缓慢滑动？
items.headline_en: Why Do Some Faults Creep Before Rupture?
items.summary: 11 月 14 日发表的实验用两块亚克力板模拟断层。研究人员给板施压，观察接触面怎样滑动。接触面较光滑时，压力较小，破裂前的缓慢滑动信号更明显；压力增大，信号就变弱。这说明能否测到前兆，也取决于断层承受的压力。
items.summary_en: In experiments published on 14 November, researchers pressed two acrylic plates together to model a fault and measured slip along their contact. On smoother surfaces, the slow-slip signal before rupture was clearer at lower pressure and weaker at higher pressure. Roughness is only part of the story.

items.headline: 太平洋变暖，为什么两侧的雨反着变？
items.headline_en: Why El Niño Shifts Rain Across the Pacific
items.summary: 美国气候预测中心 11 月 12 日报告，赤道太平洋中东部已比常年明显偏暖。暖水上方的湿空气更容易上升，云和雨随之集中到太平洋中东部；印度尼西亚一带的降雨反而偏少。海温变化可以把降雨带推向别处。
items.summary_en: On 12 November, the US Climate Prediction Center reported unusually warm water in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. Moist air rises more readily over warmer water, favouring clouds and rain farther east, while rainfall around Indonesia is suppressed. A shift in ocean temperature can move whole rain belts.

items.headline: 卫星追踪入侵植物，为什么要等它开花？
items.headline_en: Why Flowers Help Satellites Spot an Invasive Plant
items.summary: 11 月 16 日，明尼苏达大学介绍了一项用地面记录训练模型的研究：这种入侵大戟成片开黄花时，卫星图像更容易认出它。研究者用约二十年的影像追踪扩散；干旱年开花较少，地图上的空白不一定表示植物少了。
items.summary_en: On 16 November, the University of Minnesota described a model trained with ground observations. It spotted invasive leafy spurge more easily when dense patches showed yellow flowers in satellite images. The team mapped its spread using two decades of imagery; in drought years, fewer blooms can leave gaps even where plants remain.

previous_answers.headline: 选一个三位数，要求百位与个位相差至少2。把它的数字顺序倒过来，用较大的数减去较小的数。再把所得差的数字顺序倒过来，将这两个数相加。不必知道最初选的数，你能预测最后的结果吗？说明理由。（倒序后开头的0可以略去。）
previous_answers.headline_en: Choose a three-digit number whose first and last digits differ by at least 2. Reverse its digits, then subtract the smaller number from the larger. Reverse the digits of the difference and add these two numbers. Can you predict the final total without knowing the starting number? Explain why. Any leading zero in a reversed number may be omitted.
previous_answers.explanation: 设首尾数字之差为 d，则减出的数是 99d，三位数字依次为 d−1、9、10−d。倒序相加时，两端各凑成 9，中间相加得 18；进位后就是 1089。
previous_answers.explanation_en: Let d be the difference between the first and last digits. Subtracting gives 99d, whose digits are d−1, 9 and 10−d. Adding its reversal gives 9 at both ends and 18 in the middle before carrying, which gives 1,089.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 倒序数之谜解答

previous_answers.headline: 12张卡片分别写着1至12。充分洗匀后，随机抽出3张，不放回。三张卡片上的数之和能被3整除的概率是多少？请用清楚的分类计数说明答案，而不是只靠模拟。
previous_answers.headline_en: Twelve cards are numbered 1 to 12. Shuffle them thoroughly and draw three without replacement. What is the probability that their sum is divisible by 3? Explain your answer by counting cases, rather than relying only on a simulation.
previous_answers.explanation: 按除以 3 的余数分三类，每类 4 张。要使和整除，三张的余数要么全相同，要么各不相同。符合的组合有 3×4＋4³＝76 种；一共 220 种，所以是 76/220＝19/55。
previous_answers.explanation_en: There are four cards in each remainder class modulo 3. For the sum to be divisible by 3, the remainders must be all equal or all different. This gives 3×4 + 4³ = 76 valid triples out of 220, so the probability is 19/55.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 余数与概率解答

previous_answers.headline: 7名选手进行单循环比赛：每两人恰好比赛一场，每场都有一名胜者，没有平局。证明：无论比赛结果如何，总能把7人排成一列，使每个人都赢过紧挨在自己后面的人。注意：不要求一个人赢过自己后面的所有人。
previous_answers.headline_en: Seven players compete in a round-robin tournament: every pair plays exactly once, and every match has one winner, with no draws. Prove that, whatever the results, the players can always be arranged in a line so that each player beat the person immediately after them. A player need not have beaten everyone farther down the line.
previous_answers.explanation: 先排一人，再逐个加入。新选手若谁也没赢过，就放在末尾；否则把他插到队中第一位被他打败的人前面。若前面还有一人，那人一定赢过新选手，所以两个新的相邻关系都成立。
previous_answers.explanation_en: Start with one player and add the rest one at a time. If the newcomer beat nobody in the line, put them at the end. Otherwise, insert them just before the first player they beat. Any player immediately before that position must have beaten the newcomer, so both new links work.
previous_answers.subject: W46 · 胜者队列解答

challenges.headline_en: Three opaque boxes contain two red balls, two blue balls, and one of each, respectively. The three labels, “two red”, “two blue” and “one of each”, are all wrong. You may choose one box and draw one ball without looking inside. How can you identify the contents of all three boxes?
